> [!NOTE]
> Rescoped by @MatthewBonanni (1fab475): this PR now carries only the HiSparse split-read fix, done in the NIXL connector with no core change. @S1ro1's general P/D change (cache-preserving keep pauses no longer waiting on retained KV exports) moved to #59670. The original description and live RL validation are preserved there.

## Purpose

Fix a P/D pause stall with HiSparse decoders. Since #53780, a NIXL read into a decoder with mixed DRAM/VRAM KV (HiSparse) is split into one transfer per memory type, and the producer is notified only once a worker polls both done. A `pause(mode="keep")` on the decoder hides its `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` requests, so the engine stops stepping, nothing polls, and the notification is never sent. The producer keeps those blocks until its lease expires, and a keep pause on the producer waits for them.

## Changes

`NixlBaseConnectorScheduler` tracks reads it has handed to the workers (`awaiting_kvs`) until they come back in `finished_recving`, and reports them through the existing `has_pending_push_work()` hook, which `Scheduler.has_requests()` already honors. A paused decoder keeps running zero-token connector steps until its in-flight reads complete and their notifications go out.

- Failed reads and aborted waiting requests also arrive in `finished_recving`, so the set always drains.
- Unpaused behavior is unchanged: waiting requests already keep the engine stepping.
- Push mode overrides the hook and never marks a read as awaiting.

## Test Plan

- New `test_keep_pause_steps_until_remote_kv_arrives` (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py`): with a read in flight, a keep pause must keep `has_requests()` true until the receive finishes.
- NIXL / connector unit tests on CPU.
- GPU: 2×H100, shrunk DeepSeek-V3.2 (dummy weights). P is plain NIXL (pull rejects a mixed-memory producer); D is NIXL + HiSparse. A warm-up request completes the handshake; for the next request, a debug-only hook pauses D (keep) right after the step that issues its read, then the driver pauses P (keep, `clear_cache=false`).

## Test Result

The measured read is a real split read: 2 handles, 504 DRAM + 504 VRAM descriptors.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| D's pause completes | 2 ms after issuing the read, before it finishes | after the notification is sent |
| Deferred notification to P | only after D resumes (47 s) | 93 ms after the read, while pausing |
| P keep pause | **28.0 s** (lease expiry: "retrieved by 0 remote worker(s)") | **0.03 s** |
| Decode after resume | 200 | 200, same output |

- New test fails on main, passes with this PR.
- Connector unit tests: 258 passed; 2 failures also fail on main on the CPU host (engine startup / model download).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, implementation, tests, and this description.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Opened draft #59953 as an alternative approach to the split-read notification stall: each READ carries a native completion notification, and P counts the declared transfers separately for each NIXL reader agent. This removes D's deferred notification queue instead of keeping its scheduler stepping. Readers issuing zero, one, or two transfers are accounted for separately; the wire protocol version is bumped. The draft contains the core implementation only, with test updates and native/GPU validation pending. Broader receive-drain and P/D pause/resume semantics remain separate.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

@S1ro1 thanks for looking into this! :)
I believe you're attempting to address a broader "/pause-resume" PD-safety issue, which I would like to tackle at its root with a slightly broader issue.

Re: Hisparse, I actually believe this multi-xfer problem is occurring only because we're sending completion notification not on the number of xfer issued, but on the number of producers (not anymore a good proxy for that).
Lemme follow up with an alternative which standardizes to this, so that hisparse isn't different from a P TP > D TP case multi-xfer case.

files.patch:
@@ -5,6 +5,7 @@
 
 import pytest
 
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.interface import PauseState
 from vllm.v1.outputs import (
     EMPTY_MODEL_RUNNER_OUTPUT,
     KVConnectorOutput,
@@ -148,6 +149,35 @@ def test_basic_lifecycle():
     assert_scheduler_empty(scheduler)
 
 
+def test_keep_pause_steps_until_remote_kv_arrives():
+    """A paused D must keep stepping while a read is in flight: split
+    DRAM/VRAM reads notify P only once a worker polls them done."""
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config()
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(vllm_config)
+    BLOCK_SIZE = vllm_config.cache_config.block_size
+    request = create_request(
+        request_id=1,
+        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+        num_tokens=BLOCK_SIZE * 2,
+        do_remote_prefill=True,
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+    scheduler_output = scheduler.schedule()
+    scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler_output, EMPTY_MODEL_RUNNER_OUTPUT)
+    assert request.status == RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS
+
+    scheduler.set_pause_state(PauseState.PAUSED_ALL)
+    assert scheduler.has_requests()
+
+    scheduler_output = scheduler.schedule()
+    model_runner_output = copy.deepcopy(EMPTY_MODEL_RUNNER_OUTPUT)
+    model_runner_output.kv_connector_output = KVConnectorOutput(
+        finished_recving={request.request_id}
+    )
+    scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler_output, model_runner_output)
+    assert not scheduler.has_requests()
+
+
 def test_interleaved_lifecycle():
     """Test Remote Prefills Work Well With Other Requests."""
     vllm_config = create_vllm_config()

@@ -119,6 +119,10 @@ def __init__(
         # Reqs to send and their expiration time
         self._reqs_need_send: dict[ReqId, float] = {}
         self._reqs_in_batch: set[ReqId] = set()
+        # Reqs whose remote KV read was handed to the workers but has not
+        # completed. Split DRAM/VRAM reads notify P only once a worker polls
+        # them done, so the engine must keep stepping even while paused.
+        self._reqs_recving: set[ReqId] = set()
         # Reqs to remove from processed set because they're not to send after
         # remote prefill or aborted.
         self._reqs_not_processed: set[ReqId] = set()
@@ -486,6 +490,8 @@ def build_connector_meta(
             awaiting_kvs,
         ) in self._reqs_need_recv.items():
             assert req.kv_transfer_params is not None
+            if awaiting_kvs:
+                self._reqs_recving.add(req_id)
             meta.add_new_req_to_recv(
                 request_id=req_id,
                 local_block_ids=block_ids,
@@ -524,9 +530,10 @@ def update_connector_output(self, connector_output: "KVConnectorOutput") -> None
         """Stop heartbeating for requests whose KV transfer completed."""
         for req_id in connector_output.finished_recving or ():
             self._stop_heartbeat(req_id)
+            self._reqs_recving.discard(req_id)
 
     def has_pending_push_work(self) -> bool:
-        return False
+        return bool(self._reqs_recving)
 
     ############################################################
     # Abstract methods that subclasses must implement
